stem: What is the primary hormonal mechanism behind pubertal gynaecomastia in boys?

options.text: A complete lack of testosterone production in mid-puberty
Excessive intake of phytoestrogens from the diet
Peripheral aromatisation of testosterone to oestradiol
A surge in growth hormone that targets breast tissue specifically
Increased prolactin secretion from the pituitary

explanation: Peripheral aromatisation of testosterone to oestradiol is the main hormonal mechanism in pubertal gynaecomastia. During puberty, increased conversion of testosterone to oestradiol can shift the androgen-oestrogen balance and stimulate breast tissue.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because pubertal gynaecomastia is not caused by complete absence of testosterone; testosterone is present and part of the normal pubertal hormonal milieu.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because dietary phytoestrogens are not the primary mechanism of typical pubertal gynaecomastia; the key issue is endogenous hormone conversion.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because peripheral aromatisation converts testosterone to oestradiol, increasing oestrogen effect on breast tissue during puberty.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because growth hormone is not the main driver of glandular breast tissue development in pubertal gynaecomastia.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because raised prolactin is not the usual mechanism of pubertal gynaecomastia; it is more relevant in other causes of galactorrhoea or endocrine disorders.

source.hint: This process involves an enzyme that converts androgens into estrogens.
